title: P25-family depth-for-width reallocation: seven Peri-LN blocks with 3x MLPs (d_ff 768) instead of six with 4x (1024), about parameter- and FLOP-matched, on the 115-fable hybrid ALiBi/NoPE Lean incumbent (4,671,488 params)
description: Idea ID: P25-family / P24 (allocation between depth and MLP width; P01's looped depth is being tested separately by 125-fable). The only edits are N_LAYER 6 -> 7 plus 124-claude's d_ff 1024 -> 768 patch, so the model keeps ~97% of 115's parameters and matmul FLOPs but spends them on one more sequential attention+MLP step; 124 showed the fourth quarter of MLP width is worth ~0 downstream (-3.3), and expert iteration must extend cap-6 proofs to 7-14 lines, where an extra layer of citation lookup/composition should matter more than MLP lookup capacity.
hypothesis: Downstream transfer to 7+ line proofs depends on composing citations/hypotheses across more lines, which is sequential computation per token (depth), while 124-claude (6 blocks, 3x MLP: 628.00 vs 631.33, 4421 vs 4204 steps) showed the MLP's last quarter of width is not the binding resource. The Lean depth series 5/6/7 = 563/580/542 was measured on pre-Peri-LN RoPE blocks at 4x MLP, where the seventh block also added 17% parameters and cost 14% of steps (3114 vs 3607); Peri-LN is reported to make deeper stacks train better, and at 3x MLP the seventh block is roughly parameter-neutral. Prediction if right: pretraining ~3,700-3,950 steps (-6..-12% vs 4204), final val loss within 0.003 of 115 (0.080-0.087), held-out greedy >= 0.978, round-1 RL targets solved >= 700 and a 3-seed mean above 631.33 with L* >= 11. Evidence against: 102's seventh block lost 37 and 105's looped seventh application lost 34, so a seventh step may simply cost steps and RL sampling time without transfer; if so expect 590-625. Mechanism checks: steps/epochs vs 115 and 124; val and train loss vs 115; round-1 targets solved and sample acc; eval L* and the >= 10 histogram vs 115; total secs (RL sampling ~+15% slower).
expected_delta: -40 to +30 dev solves >= 7 vs 115-fable's 631.33 (central -5); pretraining steps 3,700-3,950 (115: 4204, 124: 4421), final val loss 0.080-0.087; totals 1,650-2,150 s under the 2,400 s cap

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) with Peri-LN blocks (LayerNorm on each branch output as well as its input) and hybrid attention heads, ALiBi on 4 heads and no positional signal on the other 4 (unchanged from 115-fable); CHANGED seven blocks with MLP width 3x (depth bought with MLP width)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 and 0 for heads 5..8 (NoPE); same table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: CHANGED vs 115-fable: N_LAYER 6 -> 7 and D_FF = 3 * D = 768 (124-claude's patch, applied unchanged, plus one more block). PeriLNBlock.__init__ replaces the fork Block's fc1 Linear(256,1024) / fc2 Linear(1024,256) with Linear(256,768) / Linear(768,256) (biases kept, zeroed by the fork _init, weights re-initialized orthogonally like every block matrix). muon_step's QKV role split is selected by parameter identity (qkv_ids = the seven qkv.weight tensors) instead of the shape test, which fc1 (768,256) would also pass. Attention, ALiBi/NoPE slopes (same table in all seven blocks), Peri-LN, width, embedding/readout, optimizer and schedule are identical to 115
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 7, 256, 8) from this pretrain.py, replace blocks with seven of this pretrain.py's PeriLNBlock (d_ff 768), then load state. The live harness uses the returned model object through RL and eval
arch.kv_cache: unchanged mechanism from 115-fable: one fork KV-cache dict per block (seven), ALiBi key positions in caches[0]

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, unchanged convention): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 (768,256) sqrt(3), fc2 (256,768) sqrt(3), head (107,256) 1; every Muon update has element RMS ~1/16 times lr
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 28 hidden matrices (7 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj (256,256), fc1 (768,256), fc2 (256,768)) plus head.weight
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each qkv.weight update to (3,256,256) and orthogonalize the three roles separately. Selection by identity (as in 124-claude) (id(p) in qkv_ids) instead of shape, because fc1 (768,256) now has QKV's shape; fc1 is orthogonalized as one matrix
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: CHANGED: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 29 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW
optimizer.parameters: 29 Muon matrices: 28 hidden matrices (7 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj (256,256), fc1 (768,256), fc2 (256,768)) plus head.weight

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Fork default construction (normal 0.02 embedding/readout), blocks replaced by PeriLNBlocks and re-initialized with the fork _init (zero biases), then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); output LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0 (standard Peri-LN / OLMo 2 / Gemma 2 init). RNG draws shift vs 101-claude because the blocks are built twice. At init each branch write has RMS ~1 instead of ~0.1
